I traced the loop by hand, with no code execution.

Two observations simplify it:
- `c` stays 5 throughout, because `i > 28` never holds for `i` in 0..25. So `c // 9 + c = 5`, and the line `b = (c // 9 + c) % 97` always sets `b = 5`.
- Then `b = (a - c + 9) % 97 = (a + 4) % 97`. This overwrites whatever the first branch set, so at the end of each iteration `b = (a + 4) % 97`.

The condition `(2i) % 5 == 1` holds for i ∈ {3, 8, 13, 18, 23}. On those iterations `a` is unchanged. On all others, `a = (5·b + 2) % 97`, using the `b` carried over from the previous iteration.
